summary: Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968). He subsequently served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1970 to 2008.

Indologist Katsuhiko Kamimura studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and held posts at the University of Tokyo and its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hanazono University.
Linguist Katsuji Fujioka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Historian and Japanologist Katsumi Kuroita studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896. He later held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and Hisashi Sato, INALCO, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He was long a professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

Katsumi Okimoto specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973) and served at Hanazono University as a professor (~1983–2008) and director (~2008–2014).

Katsumi Tanabe specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1968) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–2001) and Chuo University (~2001–2011).

Katsutoshi Ono specialized in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Educated at Kyoto University, he held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Nara National Museum, Kansai University, and Ryukoku University (~1964–1980).

Art historian Kavita Singh studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MSU Baroda, and Panjab University. She held posts at the College of Art, Delhi, Marg Publications, San Diego Museum of Art, and Jawaharlal Nehru University as dean.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kazi Dawa Samdup studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Lopen Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster of Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School and as a lecturer at Calcutta University.
Historian and Buddhist studies scholar Kazu Uehara studied at Kyushu University (~1947–1992). He held academic posts at the University of Miyazaki (~1951–1964) and Seijo University (~1964–1995).

Kazuaki Komine specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he held posts at Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University, where he served from 1995 to 2013.

Kazuaki Tanahashi is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow at the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing doctoral coursework at Kyoto University, he served as an assistant professor and professor emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1982–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc). He served as a professor in the Department of Geography at Kyoto University from circa 2004 to 2024.

Kazuhiko Atsumi worked in philosophy and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–2004).

Kazuhiko Yoshida studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Cornell (under Jay Jasanoff), and Osaka (under Teizo Iyanaga). A scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he held posts at Nagoya City College for Women and Kyoto University (1999–2020).
Kazuhiro Furuta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an editor and publisher at the Otani Academic Society (attested 1991) and as dean at Otani University (attested 1998).
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was affiliated with Bukkyo University, where his posts are attested in 2001 and 2013.
